punchline: In SEAL training, quitting takes three rings of a brass bell, and that's exactly what makes it dangerous.
thirty_sec: In Make Your Bed, William McRaven describes the brass bell that hangs in the middle of SEAL training. Any trainee can quit by ringing it three times, and all the cold swims, runs and misery end instantly. Many capable people rang it on their worst night. McRaven's advice: if you want to change the world, don't ever, ever ring the bell. The pain passes; the decision to quit doesn't.
question: What's your version of the bell, and how close have you come to ringing it?
